request.system: You assist requirements analysts who apply the OGORE framework. You refine one IT goal of an organization's Initial Goal Tree Model by adapting validated goal patterns retrieved from a Goal Knowledge Base. Use only the six OGORE element types: Goal, Task, Resource, Actor, Belief, Constraint. Do not invent KPI values.

messages.content:
RETRIEVED PATTERNS:
[SKB-07/G2] (similarity 0.7171)
PATTERN SKB-07 | hospital pharmacy (synthetic) | medicine handling; expiry and dispensing control
Organization goal: dispense safe medicines without waste from expiry
IT goal G2: Expiry dates controlled (parent G1, AND)
  KPIs: G2-K1 Items picked first-expiry-first-out (target 100%); G2-K2 Expired items removed from stock (target within 1 day of expiry)
  Tasks: Record batch and expiry at receipt; Suggest picking by earliest expiry; Report items expiring within 90 days
  Resources: Pharmacy stock module
  Actors: Pharmacist in Charge; Pharmacy Technician
  Beliefs: Regulation requires batch records for every medicine
  Constraints: Only a pharmacist may release quarantined medicines
  Rational statement: Batch and expiry captured at receipt make both FEFO picking and recalls possible.

[SKB-01/G2] (similarity 0.5187)
PATTERN SKB-01 | medium-sized food and beverage distributor (synthetic) | wholesale distribution; order-to-cash and lot traceability
Organization goal: deliver complete and traceable orders to retail customers
IT goal G2: Customer orders recorded accurately (parent G1, AND)
  KPIs: G2-K1 Order lines matching the customer purchase order (target 99.5%); G2-K2 Order confirmation sent after entry (target within 30 minutes)
  Tasks: Capture customer purchase order with price list validation; Confirm order to customer
  Resources: Customer price list; Order management module
  Actors: Sales Administrator; Customer
  Beliefs: Price lists are customer specific
  Constraints: A confirmed order cannot be edited without a change request
  Conflict resolved: lot scanning slows picking and delays confirmation -> confirm the order at entry and scan lots at picking, so confirmation time is unaffected

[SKB-01/G3] (similarity 0.4972)
PATTERN SKB-01 | medium-sized food and beverage distributor (synthetic) | wholesale distribution; order-to-cash and lot traceability
Organization goal: deliver complete and traceable orders to retail customers
IT goal G3: Lot numbers traceable from receipt to customer (parent G1, AND)
  KPIs: G3-K1 Shipped lines with lot number recorded (target 100%); G3-K2 Time to list all customers of a recalled lot (target under 4 hours)
  Tasks: Scan lot number at goods receipt; Record lot number on each picked line; Run recall trace report
  Resources: Barcode scanners; Lot master data
  Actors: Warehouse Clerk; Quality Officer
  Beliefs: Suppliers print lot numbers on every carton
  Constraints: A line without a lot number cannot be shipped
  Rational statement: Lot capture at receipt and picking makes a recall trace a query instead of a manual search, which is what the 4-hour KPI requires.
  Conflict resolved: lot scanning slows picking and delays confirmation -> confirm the order at entry and scan lots at picking, so confirmation time is unaffected

[SKB-02/G2] (similarity 0.47)
PATTERN SKB-02 | cold-chain logistics provider for frozen food (synthetic) | temperature-controlled warehousing and transport
Organization goal: keep every temperature-controlled shipment within its specified range
IT goal G2: Temperature excursions detected and handled (parent G1, AND)
  KPIs: G2-K1 Cold shipments with a continuous temperature log (target 100%); G2-K2 Excursion alerts acknowledged (target within 30 minutes)
  Tasks: Stream logger readings to the monitoring service; Alert the duty supervisor on an excursion; Quarantine affected goods pending a release decision
  Resources: Temperature data loggers; Monitoring dashboard
  Actors: Duty Supervisor; Quality Manager
  Beliefs: Loggers record every five minutes
  Constraints: Goods with an unresolved excursion cannot be released
  Rational statement: A release decision by the Quality Manager is the control that turns a detected excursion into a safe outcome.
  Conflict resolved: automatic release would speed dispatch but bypass quality review -> automatic release only for excursions under 15 minutes and 2 degrees; all others need the Quality Manager

QUERY:
GOAL: G03 "Batch and expiry traceable to each hospital"; parent G01 "Regulated order-to-delivery controlled and secure"
DOMAIN: pharmaceutical distribution to hospitals; organization type: medium-sized distributor with an order portal and an LLM-based ordering assistant
KPIS: G03-K1 = Shipped lines with batch number and expiry date recorded (100%); G03-K2 = Time to list every hospital that received a recalled batch (under 2 hours)
ACTORS IN SCOPE: Hospital Buyer; Sales Administrator; Responsible Pharmacist; Quality Assurance Officer; IT Security Officer; Data Protection Officer; AI Product Owner
BELIEFS: Good distribution practice requires batch records for every medicine
CONSTRAINTS: A line without batch and expiry cannot be shipped

TASK: (1) Rank the retrieved patterns by relevance to the query and state why each is relevant, citing its pattern ID. (2) Adapt them to the query and propose Tasks, Actors, Resources, Beliefs, and Constraints for the goal (and sub-goals only if the goal needs further decomposition). (3) Link every proposed element to the goal ID or to one of its KPI IDs, exactly as given in the query. (4) Draft one rational statement that explains how the goal and its elements serve the parent goal and its KPIs. (5) Give, for each element, the pattern ID it was adapted from; if it was not taken from a retrieved pattern, write UNGROUNDED. Every proposed element must respect the beliefs and constraints listed in the query.

ranked_patterns.relevance: Most relevant structurally: its IT goal 'Lot numbers traceable from receipt to customer' mirrors G03 almost one-to-one, and both of its KPIs map directly onto the query KPIs (shipped lines with lot number 100% -> G03-K1; time to list customers of a recalled lot -> G03-K2, tightened from 4h to 2h). Its tasks (scan at receipt, record on each picked line, recall trace report), its constraint 'a line without a lot number cannot be shipped' and its Quality Officer actor transfer to pharmaceutical distribution with batch+expiry replacing lot.

Highest textual similarity and the only pattern from a regulated medicine domain: it supplies the expiry dimension that SKB-01/G3 lacks (record batch and expiry at receipt, FEFO picking, expiry horizon reporting), the belief 'Regulation requires batch records for every medicine' which matches the query belief on good distribution practice, and the constraint that only a pharmacist may release quarantined medicines, adapted here to the Responsible Pharmacist.

Relevant as the sibling order-entry goal from the same order-to-cash pattern: it contributes the Sales Administrator and Customer actors (adapted to Hospital Buyer), the order management module as the system of record where batch allocation is attached, the constraint on changing confirmed orders, and above all the recorded conflict resolution (confirm at entry, scan lots at picking) that keeps batch/expiry capture from degrading order confirmation time under the parent goal.

Least directly aligned (it targets temperature excursions, not identification data), but it is the only pattern that models the handling branch after a problem is detected: quarantine pending a release decision, a named quality role owning that decision, and a constraint forbidding release while unresolved. These are reused to make a recall triggered by G03-K2 end in a controlled block-and-release outcome rather than only a list of hospitals.

elements.text: Scan batch number and expiry date at goods receipt and bind them to the received stock record
elements.justification: Combines 'Scan lot number at goods receipt' (SKB-01/G3) with 'Record batch and expiry at receipt' (SKB-07/G2); capturing both identifiers at the earliest point is the precondition for 100% recorded shipped lines and respects the belief that every medicine needs a batch record.

elements.text: Record batch number and expiry date on every picked line before shipment confirmation
elements.justification: Direct adaptation of 'Record lot number on each picked line'; extended with expiry because the query KPI G03-K1 requires both attributes on 100% of shipped lines.

elements.text: Block dispatch of any order line whose batch number or expiry date is missing or does not match the stock record
elements.justification: Operationalises the pattern constraint 'a line without a lot number cannot be shipped' and the query constraint, turning it into an enforceable system check that protects the 100% target.

elements.text: Allocate stock to hospital orders by earliest expiry first (FEFO) and flag lines whose remaining shelf life is below the hospital's accepted minimum
elements.justification: Adapted from 'Suggest picking by earliest expiry'; FEFO allocation makes the recorded expiry data actionable and keeps expired or near-expired medicines out of hospital deliveries.

elements.text: Run a recall trace query that lists every hospital, order and shipped line for a given batch number
elements.justification: Direct adaptation of 'Run recall trace report'; the report is the mechanism that makes the under-2-hour KPI a database query instead of a manual reconstruction.

elements.text: Quarantine remaining stock of a recalled or suspect batch and hold it pending a documented release decision
elements.justification: Adapted from 'Quarantine affected goods pending a release decision' (SKB-02/G2) and the pharmacist release control (SKB-07/G2), so a trace result ends in a controlled disposition rather than only a list.

elements.text: Report batches held in stock or already shipped that expire within 90 days to the Quality Assurance Officer
elements.justification: Adapted from 'Report items expiring within 90 days'; turns captured expiry data into preventive action consistent with good distribution practice.

elements.text: Validate any batch or product reference proposed by the LLM-based ordering assistant against batch master data and reject unmatched references before the order line is created
elements.justification: No retrieved pattern covers an LLM ordering assistant; the check is required so that assistant-generated lines cannot introduce batch or expiry values that break G03-K1 or the shipping constraint.

elements.text: Confirm the hospital order at entry and capture batch and expiry at picking, so confirmation time is unaffected by scanning
elements.justification: Reuses the recorded conflict resolution in SKB-01/G2 (lot scanning slows picking and delays confirmation) so traceability work does not degrade the order-to-delivery performance expected by parent goal G01.

elements.text: Batch and expiry master data (batch number, expiry date, product, supplier, received quantity)
elements.justification: Adapted from 'Lot master data' (SKB-01/G3), extended with the expiry attribute from the pharmacy stock module (SKB-07/G2); it is the single reference both KPIs are computed against.

elements.text: Barcode or 2D-code scanners at receipt and picking stations
elements.justification: Direct reuse of 'Barcode scanners'; scanning rather than keying is what makes 100% recorded batch and expiry realistic at picking speed.

elements.text: Warehouse stock module with batch- and expiry-level inventory tracking
elements.justification: Adapted from 'Pharmacy stock module'; batch-level inventory is needed to hold expiry per batch, support FEFO and quarantine a specific batch.

elements.text: Order management module and order portal holding the hospital-to-shipped-line link
elements.justification: Adapted from 'Order management module'; the hospital/order/line linkage stored here is what the recall trace joins to batch data to answer G03-K2.

elements.text: Recall trace report with batch-to-hospital query and exportable audit log
elements.justification: The pattern task 'Run recall trace report' presupposes a reporting artefact; it is made explicit as a resource because the 2-hour KPI is measured on its response.

elements.text: Sales Administrator
elements.justification: Pattern actor reused unchanged; records and confirms hospital order lines to which batch allocation is later attached, and handles change requests on confirmed lines.

elements.text: Responsible Pharmacist
elements.justification: Adapted from 'Pharmacist in Charge'; is the only role entitled to release quarantined batches after a recall trace, as required by the pattern constraint and by good distribution practice.

elements.text: Quality Assurance Officer
elements.justification: Adapted from the Quality Officer (SKB-01/G3) and Quality Manager (SKB-02/G2); owns the recall trace execution, the quarantine decision file and the expiry-horizon review.

elements.text: Hospital Buyer
elements.justification: Adapted from the 'Customer' actor; is the recipient identified by the trace and the party notified of a recalled batch, which is why the hospital-line link must be kept complete.

elements.text: AI Product Owner
elements.justification: Not present in any retrieved pattern; accountable for the ordering assistant's validation behaviour so that assistant-created lines never bypass batch and expiry capture.

elements.text: Data Protection Officer
elements.justification: Not present in any retrieved pattern; recall trace output contains hospital customer data, so its disclosure scope needs an accountable owner under the parent goal's security concern.

elements.text: Good distribution practice requires a batch record for every medicine shipped
elements.justification: Stated in the query and matching the pattern belief 'Regulation requires batch records for every medicine'; it justifies why G03-K1 is set at 100% rather than a tolerance.

elements.text: Suppliers print a readable batch number and expiry date on every carton delivered
elements.justification: Adapted from 'Suppliers print lot numbers on every carton'; scanning at receipt only yields 100% coverage if this holds, so it is recorded as an explicit assumption.

elements.text: Batch and expiry values proposed by the LLM ordering assistant are suggestions and are not authoritative until matched against batch master data
elements.justification: Specific to the organization's LLM-based assistant; no retrieved pattern addresses generated data, and the belief is needed to justify the validation task.

elements.text: A line without a recorded batch number and expiry date cannot be shipped
elements.justification: Query constraint, identical in form to the pattern constraint 'a line without a lot number cannot be shipped'; it is the hard rule that guarantees the 100% target.

elements.text: Only the Responsible Pharmacist may release a quarantined batch; a batch with an unresolved recall or quality hold cannot be shipped
elements.justification: Merges 'Only a pharmacist may release quarantined medicines' (SKB-07/G2) with 'Goods with an unresolved excursion cannot be released' (SKB-02/G2), adapted to recall holds.

elements.text: Batch allocation on a confirmed order line cannot be changed without a recorded change request
elements.justification: Adapted from 'A confirmed order cannot be edited without a change request'; prevents silent re-allocation that would break the hospital-to-batch audit trail used by G03-K2.

elements.text: Recall trace output containing hospital identities may be disclosed only to the Responsible Pharmacist, Quality Assurance Officer and authorised recipients, and every access is logged
elements.justification: No retrieved pattern addresses data protection; required because the parent goal G01 demands that the regulated order-to-delivery chain also be secure.

output.rational_statement: Capturing batch number and expiry at goods receipt and re-confirming them on every picked line, with dispatch blocked when either is missing, makes G03-K1 a by-product of normal receipt and picking work rather than a separate compliance effort, while the shared batch and expiry master data turns the recall question behind G03-K2 into a single query over the order portal's hospital-to-line link instead of a manual document search, so the under-2-hour target is met and the result can be acted on immediately through quarantine and a Responsible Pharmacist release decision; because batch and expiry are scanned at picking while the hospital order is confirmed at entry, this traceability adds no delay to order confirmation, and because trace output is access-restricted and logged, G03 supports both halves of parent goal G01 'Regulated order-to-delivery controlled and secure' - regulatory control through complete, FEFO-consistent batch records validated even when lines originate from the LLM ordering assistant, and security through governed disclosure of the hospital data that traceability necessarily exposes.
